minutes.headline: Board approved diner license transfer and dispatch expansion; manager zeroed pavement line for balance, offset by Chapter 90 rise.
minutes.summary: Only two Select Board members were in the room, with a third on Zoom, so licenses and minutes could not be signed. The board heard assessor warrant articles on tax exemptions, a vendor fair presentation and the town manager's report. The manager described the preliminary budget, with pavement management cut to zero and a higher Chapter 90 apportionment. The board voted on the diner license, Hudson joining regional dispatch and surplus sand, then went into executive session.

The town received its Chapter 90 apportionment, substantially higher than prior years. It depends on a state bond authorization.

what_happened.line: The board approved the common victualler license transfer for Lunenburg Diner by roll call, but it cannot be signed until a third member signs.
The board voted to authorize the town manager to sign the revised regional 911 dispatch agreement adding Hudson, passing unanimously.
The manager said the preliminary budget sets the pavement management line at zero to balance it, and will add a placeholder warrant article for one-time funds.
The town's Chapter 90 apportionment was described as substantially higher than prior years, and it depends on a state bond authorization.
No decision was reached on the right of first refusal for 100 Townsend Harbor Road; it was deferred to a full board, before the warrant closes.

why_it_matters: Road repair funding in the preliminary budget now depends on a separate warrant article using one-time money such as free cash, so residents may be asked to vote on it at town meeting.
Buying 100 Townsend Harbor Road would, by the manager's account, change the capital program and leave FY27 with no starting free cash, so the decision touches future budgets as well as this one.
watch_next: A decision on the right of first refusal for 100 Townsend Harbor Road, which must be made before the warrant closes.
The placeholder pavement management warrant article, and whether town counsel says the COLA must be stated in the exemption article language.
